subtopics.title: International Relations and Trade
subtopics.summary: This group covers the Durand Line, the 2,600 km boundary between Pakistan and Afghanistan that was fixed by a British-era agreement and has been contested since Partition. It also covers India's trade agreements with New Zealand and Oman expand trade and investment, with zero-duty access stated only for New Zealand. The section closes with the US National Security Strategy, the Preah Vihear temple dispute, and India's re-election to the IMO Council.
facts: The Durand Line is a 2,600 km international boundary between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
It was drawn through the Durand Agreement of 1893 between Sir Henry Mortimer Durand and Emir Abdur Rahman Khan.
Afghanistan refused to formally recognise the Durand Line, viewing it as a colonial imposition.
Treaty of Gandamak (1879) granted Britain control over Afghanistan's foreign affairs.
Treaty of Rawalpindi (1919) restored Afghanistan's foreign policy autonomy while reaffirming the Durand Line.
India-New Zealand FTA gives 100% of Indian exports to New Zealand zero-duty market access.
India-Oman CEPA is India's second CEPA in the GCC after the UAE and aims to expand trade beyond USD 10 billion.
US National Security Strategy reasserts the Monroe Doctrine (1823) and avoids branding Russia and China as existential threats.
ICJ (1962) gave sovereignty over Preah Vihear Temple to Cambodia; the 2013 ICJ clarification called for a demilitarised zone that was never fully implemented.
India was re-elected to the IMO Council's Category B for 2026-27 with the highest votes.

subtopics.title: Rights, Governance and Society
subtopics.summary: This group covers the Karbi Anglong unrest, where protests over land and resource rights under the Sixth Schedule have caused civilian deaths and internet shutdowns. It also covers the proposed Right to Disconnect, the Supreme Court's ruling on workplace harassment complaints under the PoSH framework, and Assam's proposal to grant ST status to six communities. The section ends with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and Human Rights Day.
facts: Karbi Anglong unrest began with a hunger strike by indigenous tribal groups.
Protesters demanded eviction of long-settled non-tribal communities from protected grazing and tribal lands.
Karbi Anglong is administered by the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council under the Sixth Schedule.
The Karbi Anglong Peace Accord 2021 was a tripartite agreement involving the Government of India, Assam and Karbi insurgent groups.
The Right to Disconnect would give employees a statutory right to refuse work calls, emails or messages beyond work hours and on holidays.
France's El Khomri Law (2017) was the first national law recognising the right to disconnect.
The Supreme Court (Sohail Malik case) held that women can approach the ICC at their own workplace over harassment by outsiders.
An Internal Complaints Committee is mandatory in every workplace employing 10 or more persons; a Local Committee applies where none exists.
Assam's Group of Ministers recommended ST status for 6 communities; ST (Plains) has 10% reservation and ST (Hills) has 5%.
The UDHR (1948) is not a legally binding treaty but forms the International Bill of Human Rights; Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December.

subtopics.title: Economy, Finance and Insurance
subtopics.summary: The RBI's National Strategy for Financial Inclusion 2025-30 sets out five pillars for widening access to financial services over the next five years. The section also explains masala bonds, which let Indian entities raise rupee-denominated debt overseas, and how taxes, cesses and surcharges differ in their use and sharing with states. Recent bills on a health-security cess and on insurance FDI complete the section.
facts: The National Strategy for Financial Inclusion 2025-30 was released by the RBI after approval by a Sub-Committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council.
The strategy defines 5 key pillars to guide India's financial inclusion roadmap for the next five years.
The pillars cover equitable access, gender-sensitive inclusion, linking livelihoods and skills, financial education, and customer protection.
The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) enabled the opening of over 56 crore bank accounts.
Masala bonds are rupee-denominated debt issued in overseas markets; the IFC introduced them in 2014 on the London Stock Exchange.
The RBI governs masala bonds.
A cess is used only for its earmarked purpose, while a surcharge adds to Union revenue with no specific purpose.
Taxes are shared with states through the Divisible Pool.
The Health Security and National Security Cess Bill 2025 introduces a capacity-based excise cess; initial coverage includes Pan Masala.
The Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill 2025 raises the FDI limit in Indian insurance companies from 74% to 100%.

subtopics.title: Environment, Energy and Disaster
subtopics.summary: India's updated seismic zonation map under the BIS 2025 Earthquake Design Code places the entire Himalayan arc in the new highest-risk Zone VI. The section also covers the SHANTI Bill 2025 for nuclear energy, CITES CoP20 and its appendix system, and UNEA-7, where India's wildfire resolution was adopted. The International Big Cat Alliance rounds out the wildlife items.
facts: The new Zone VI is the highest-risk zone and covers the entire Himalayan arc for the first time.
Towns located on boundaries between zones now automatically fall into the higher-risk zone.
75% of India's population lives in seismically active regions.
The National Center for Seismology operates the National Seismological Network and monitors earthquakes in real time.
The SHANTI Bill 2025 would replace the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010.
CITES was signed on 3 March 1973 and came into force on 1 July 1975; CoP20 was held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
CITES Appendix I lists species threatened with extinction, where commercial trade is prohibited; Appendix II allows controlled trade.
UNEA-7 was held in Nairobi in 2025, and India's resolution on strengthening global wildfire management was adopted there.
Over 36% of India's forests are prone to frequent fires, according to the India State of Forest Report 2021.
The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in 2023 to celebrate 50 years of Project Tiger and aims to conserve 7 big cat species.

subtopics.title: History, Heritage and Health
subtopics.summary: This group traces Vande Mataram from its 1875 composition and the 1937 limit to two stanzas to its 1950 status as national song. It also covers Deepavali's 2025 UNESCO listing, the Goa Liberation Day commemoration, and the 25 December birth anniversaries of Vajpayee and Malaviya. The health item tracks India's HIV/AIDS response through NACP V and the 2024 figures.
facts: Vande Mataram was written in 1875 by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and was published in the 1882 novel Anandamath.
A 1937 Congress Working Committee decision limited national use of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas.
On 24 January 1950, Dr Rajendra Prasad declared Vande Mataram the national song, to be honoured equally with the national anthem.
Unlike the national anthem, Vande Mataram is not enforceable under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971.
Deepavali was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2025; India's total entries now stand at 16.
Goa Liberation Day on 19 December commemorates Operation Vijay (1961), which ended 451 years of Portuguese rule.
Goa attained full statehood on 30 May 1987, becoming India's 25th state.
Atal Bihari Vajpayee (born 25 December 1924) and Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya (born 25 December 1861) are honoured on their birth anniversaries, which mark Good Governance Day.
NACP V (2021-2026) is a central sector scheme aligned with SDG 3.3 to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
HIV prevalence declined from 0.33% in 2010 to 0.20% in 2024, and new infections fell from 1.25 lakh to 64,500 over the same period.

quizzes.passage:
Unrest in Karbi Anglong, the largest district of Assam, has renewed debate on land and resource rights. The current instability began with a hunger strike by indigenous tribal groups, who demanded the eviction of long-settled non-tribal communities. Protesters argue that these settlements in protected grazing and tribal lands are unconstitutional and illegal. The district is administered by an autonomous council that works under a constitutional scheme giving autonomy to tribal areas in the North-East. A tripartite peace accord signed in 2021 aimed to end decades of insurgency and promised the council greater legislative, executive and administrative powers.

Workplace rights are also under debate. A private member's bill introduced in the Lok Sabha seeks to give employees a statutory right to refuse work calls, emails or messages beyond working hours and on holidays. Such bills are introduced by MPs who are not ministers, and their passage is uncommon. Constant digital availability is linked to anxiety, sleep-related disorders and burnout.

Harassment complaints form another part of this debate. A Supreme Court judgment held that a woman can approach the Internal Complaints Committee at her own workplace when the harasser is an outsider. The ruling expands the jurisdiction of the law on sexual harassment at work, which is based on guidelines issued by the Supreme Court. Its aim is to prevent, prohibit and redress harassment, and it applies to all women irrespective of employment status.

quizzes.passage:
The Assam Group of Ministers has recommended Scheduled Tribe status for a group of communities, a move that would be a significant step toward inclusion for them. Scheduled Tribe status is granted to groups identified under the Constitution, and the President holds the authority to notify the initial list. Any later revision of that list needs approval from Parliament. The proposal would create a new category called ST (Valley), and all such communities would fall under a National ST List. Until formal approval, the ministers have suggested a temporary relief in the form of sub-categorising the existing OBC quota within the state.

The move is described as a major inclusion step, but it has not yet been formally approved. At present, Assam has two ST segments. ST (Plains) carries a reservation of ten per cent, while ST (Hills) carries a smaller share. The proposal is therefore significant for reservation policy in the state.

The debate on workplace rights has its own constitutional roots. A proposed Right to Disconnect is linked to the right to dignity and a life with meaningful rest. The Constitution also directs the State to protect workers' health and to create humane and safe working conditions. Such a law would give employees a statutory right to refuse work messages beyond work hours and on holidays.

quizzes.passage:
India has updated its seismic zonation map under the Earthquake Design Code of 2025, factoring in fault lines, tectonics and historical earthquake data. The revised map places the entire Himalayan arc in a new highest-risk zone for the first time. Towns located on the boundaries between zones will now automatically fall into the higher-risk category. The approach shifts focus from administrative boundaries to geological conditions, with stronger emphasis on active faults and the behaviour of rock and soil. This matters because a large part of the population lives in seismically active regions.

Forests face a growing threat from fire. According to the India State of Forest Report 2021, over 36 per cent of forests are prone to frequent fires. Governments have responded with schemes that support states in managing forest fires. At UNEA-7 in Nairobi, India's resolution on strengthening global wildfire management was adopted.

Nuclear energy is also being reformed. A bill introduced in the Lok Sabha would open the sector to private companies and joint ventures with government entities. It would give the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board statutory status and create an advisory council to hear appeals against decisions of the Central Government and the regulator. Under the bill, the nuclear liability framework would move to a tiered structure based on reactor capacity.

quizzes.passage:
The International Big Cat Alliance is a multi-country coalition that aims to conserve the world's large wild cats. It was set up to mark a major anniversary of India's tiger conservation programme. Its implementing body is a national authority under the environment ministry, and its secretariat is based in New Delhi. Countries where big cats live are invited to join, and any member of the United Nations is eligible.

The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species is a legally binding agreement that regulates global trade in wild fauna and flora. It was signed in Washington, and it aims to ensure that trade does not threaten the survival of species. The agreement does not replace national laws, so countries must pass domestic legislation to enforce it. Its appendices divide species according to the level of trade control they need.

Wildfire management also features in global talks. The United Nations Environment Assembly held its seventh session in Kenya in 2025, with the theme of a resilient planet. At that session, India's resolution on wildfire management was adopted. It calls for early warning systems, community-focused alert mechanisms and joint frameworks for prevention and recovery. It also supports national and regional action plans for integrated fire management, and it encourages the sharing of best practices among countries.

quizzes.passage:
Parliament has scheduled a special discussion to commemorate 150 years of the national song, Vande Mataram. The song was composed as a patriotic response to the British promotion of a royal anthem. It was first published in a Bengali novel, and it later became the rallying cry of the Swadeshi movement after the Partition of Bengal. A decision of the Congress Working Committee in 1937 limited its national use to the first two stanzas, and that decision has been debated since. On 24 January 1950, the song was declared the national song, to be honoured equally with the national anthem.

Health policy is also part of this section. The National AIDS Control Programme aims at the prevention, control and management of HIV/AIDS in India. Its current phase is a central sector scheme that aligns with global development goals to end AIDS as a public health threat by a target year. Between 2010 and 2024, national HIV prevalence declined, and new infections fell sharply.

Heritage recognition also covers living traditions. Deepavali was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list, which seeks to safeguard knowledge, practices and traditions passed across generations. The list has categories such as oral traditions, performing arts, social practices and traditional craftsmanship. Such recognition is intended to ensure that these traditions continue to be practised.

quizzes.passage:
Good Governance Day is marked on 25 December, the birth anniversary of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He served as Prime Minister for three terms and became the first non-Congress Prime Minister to complete a full term. During his government, India conducted nuclear tests, and a major highway project was launched to connect important cities. He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and later with the Bharat Ratna.

The same day honours Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, who was a Congress president on several occasions. He founded a university in Varanasi and a Hindi weekly named Abhyudaya. He was also associated with the Hindu Mahasabha, which he helped establish.

Goa's history is marked by a long period of Portuguese rule. After Indian armed forces acted in 1961, Goa, Daman and Diu became a union territory. Portugal later formally recognised Indian sovereignty over these territories through a treaty. Goa eventually attained full statehood, and it has since been one of India's states.

The National AIDS Control Programme is in its fifth phase, which is a central sector scheme. The phase aligns with a Sustainable Development Goal that targets ending AIDS as a public health threat. Between 2010 and 2024, national HIV prevalence declined, and new infections fell by nearly half. The programme is implemented by the National AIDS Control Organisation under the health ministry.
